title: 🚀 Mission to Mars
theme: Build your own satellite company and make space accessible
description: You've been accepted into the elite Youth Space Entrepreneur Program! With 500 Mento Coins in startup funding, build and operate your own satellite company. Choose your mission, invest in technology, and navigate the challenges of the space industry. Make your mark among the stars!

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: Read each space industry scenario and decide how to grow your satellite company
Choose missions, invest in research, and make strategic technology decisions
Track your Mento Coins, Research Points, and Satellites Deployed across rounds
Balance risk-taking with careful financial management -- space ventures are expensive!
Build your Industry Reputation and complete Successful Missions to become a space mogul
tips: Invest in Research Points early -- they unlock better satellite technology and mission options
High risk missions offer bigger rewards but can drain your budget if they fail
Keep your Reputation high to attract better contracts and partnerships

learning_objectives: Evaluate different space industry business models including communications satellites, earth observation, debris cleanup, and cargo delivery
Make technology investment decisions by weighing cost, reliability, and innovation potential across off-the-shelf, experimental, and hybrid approaches
Understand launch logistics and cost optimization by comparing rideshare, dedicated, university partnership, and experimental launch methods
Develop strategic thinking and risk assessment skills in a high-stakes industry where failures are costly but innovation is essential
Build financial literacy by managing startup funding, research budgets, and revenue streams in a capital-intensive space venture

player_profile.name: Space Entrepreneur
player_profile.background: Selected for elite youth space program with big ambitions

rounds.title: Round 1: Mission Selection
rounds.story:
Welcome to the Youth Space Entrepreneur Program!

You have {{mento_coins}} Mento Coins in startup funding. Your first critical decision: What will your satellites DO?

Each mission type requires different technology, serves different markets, and faces unique challenges:

🌐 **Communications**: Provide internet to remote areas (Steady income, moderate risk)
🌍 **Earth Observation**: Monitor climate and disasters (Research grants, high impact)
🗑️ **Space Debris Cleanup**: Revolutionary! (High risk, potential for major contracts)
📦 **Cargo Delivery**: Transport supplies to space stations (Logistics focus, existing demand)
rounds.goal: Choose your company's primary mission focus

choices.label: Communications Network
choices.description: Build satellites providing internet and phone service to remote areas. Proven technology with real customers waiting. Steady revenue stream.
choices.feedback: Communications it is! Solid business case. You'll provide internet to underserved regions while building sustainable revenue.

choices.label: Earth Observation & Climate
choices.description: Deploy satellites to monitor climate, agriculture, disasters. High social impact. Research grants available from governments and universities.
choices.feedback: Earth observation chosen! Scientists and governments need your data. Purpose meets profit in climate research.

choices.label: Space Debris Cleanup
choices.description: Experimental mission collecting space junk. Nobody's solved it yet. Risky but revolutionary. Potential for major contracts if successful.
choices.feedback: Bold choice! Space debris is a growing crisis. If you succeed, you'll be famous. If you fail... well, you'll learn a lot trying!

choices.label: Cargo Delivery Service
choices.description: Transport supplies to space stations and moon bases. Logistics-focused business. Contracts already waiting. The 'Amazon of space'.
choices.feedback: Logistics path chosen! Space stations need constant resupply. Reliable, growing market with clear demand.

rounds.image_prompt: a vibrant space-themed room filled with holographic displays showcasing satellite designs, colorful charts on walls, and a large interactive screen highlighting mission options, bright lighting
rounds.coaching_moment: Consider how this choice affects your long-term resources, not just the immediate gain.
rounds.reflection_prompt: What tradeoff did this decision reveal? What did you gain, and what did you give up?

expert_pick.reason: Resilience research shows that processing setbacks openly builds stronger teams.

rounds.title: Round 2: Technology Platform
rounds.story:
Now you need to BUILD your satellite.

Current funds: {{mento_coins}} MC
Mission: Your chosen specialty

Three technology approaches:

📦 **Off-the-Shelf Components** (200 MC): Tested, reliable, standard capabilities
🔬 **Experimental Tech** (300 MC): University partnership, cutting-edge, high performance but risky
🛠️ **DIY Modular Design** (150 MC): Custom build from open-source plans, cheaper but needs more testing
⚖️ **Hybrid Approach** (250 MC): Reliable core + innovative add-ons, balanced risk-reward

choices.label: Proven Off-the-Shelf (200 MC)
choices.description: Buy tested components from established suppliers. Safe, reliable, standard capabilities. Won't break records but won't break down.
choices.feedback: Commercial components purchased. Tested and reliable. Sometimes boring is beautiful in space!

choices.label: Experimental Technology (300 MC)
choices.description: Partner with university research lab for advanced prototype systems. Revolutionary ion drive! If it works, most advanced small satellite ever built.
choices.feedback: University partnership formed! Their new ion drive is untested but revolutionary. You're pioneering the future!

choices.label: DIY Modular Design (150 MC)
choices.description: Build custom system from open-source plans. Cheaper, requires expertise, needs more testing. You'll understand every component intimately.
choices.feedback: DIY approach chosen! Using open-source specs and creativity. Risky but you'll know this satellite inside-out.

choices.label: Hybrid Approach (250 MC)
choices.description: Mix proven core systems with innovative add-ons. Balanced risk-reward. Safety AND innovation through strategic engineering.
choices.feedback: Brilliant compromise! Reliable core + experimental components you can update. Safety AND innovation!

rounds.image_prompt: a vibrant workshop filled with blueprints and satellite parts, tools scattered around, sunlight streaming through large windows, an atmosphere of creativity and innovation
rounds.coaching_moment: Think about trade-offs: what are you giving up to get this benefit?

expert_pick.reason: The most effective leaders adapt their approach based on the situation — not habit.

rounds.title: Round 3: Launch Strategy
rounds.story:
Your satellite is built! Stats:
• Funds: {{mento_coins}} MC
• Satellites ready: {{satellites_deployed}}
• Reputation: {{reputation}}%

Now the expensive part: Getting to orbit!

🚀 **Rideshare** (180 MC): Share SpaceX rocket, cheaper, less control
🎯 **Dedicated Launcher** (350 MC): Your own small rocket, complete control
⏳ **University Launch** (0 MC): Free but 6-12 month wait
🎈 **Balloon Deploy** (80 MC): Experimental near-space approach
rounds.setting: Launch Planning - 6 Weeks to Launch Window

choices.label: Rideshare on SpaceX (180 MC)
choices.description: Share Falcon 9 with 30 other small satellites. Economical choice. Launch in 6 weeks but less control over orbit.
choices.feedback: Rideshare booked! Smart, economical. You'll share the rocket but the mission is yours. Launch in 6 weeks!

choices.label: Dedicated Small Rocket (350 MC)
choices.description: Book entire Rocket Lab rocket. Expensive but you choose exact orbit and timing. Premium service for premium price.
choices.feedback: Dedicated launch booked! Complete control over when and where. Your satellite exactly where you need it!

choices.label: University Partnership (0 MC)
choices.description: Partner with university space program for free launch. Zero cost but might wait 6-12 months. Use time for testing and customer development.
choices.feedback: University partnership secured! Free launch but you'll wait. Meanwhile, test systems and build customer relationships. Patience pays!

choices.label: High-Altitude Balloon (80 MC)
choices.description: Experimental: High-altitude balloon to near-space. Not technically orbit, but perfect for your mission. Pioneering low-cost space access!
choices.feedback: Revolutionary approach! Near-space deployment is perfect for your mission. You're pioneering new low-cost methods!

rounds.image_prompt: a bustling space launch facility with a sleek rocket on the launch pad, engineers in bright uniforms discussing plans, sunlight glinting off metal surfaces, an air of excitement
rounds.coaching_moment: How might your team react to this decision? What about your customers?
rounds.reflection_prompt: Why did you choose this option? What were you trying to protect or grow?

expert_pick.reason: Resilience research shows that processing setbacks openly builds stronger teams.

glossary_terms.definition: A spacecraft placed in orbit around Earth (or other body) to collect information or provide services like communications, navigation, or observation.
glossary_terms.example: GPS satellites help you navigate. Communications satellites enable global internet and phone service.

glossary_terms.definition: The price to launch a payload into orbit, typically measured in cost per kilogram. Launch costs are the single biggest expense for space companies.
glossary_terms.example: SpaceX revolutionized space by reducing launch costs from $10,000/kg to under $3,000/kg through reusable rockets.
